summary: The Independent examines Jada Pinkett Smith's October 2023 revelation that she and Will Smith have been separated since 2016, and asks when couples should divorce rather than stay separated. Relationship experts Susan Winter and Jacob Lucas offer contrasting views on long separations, promises never to divorce, and signs a marriage is over. The piece also recounts the couple's past statements on divorce, their lack of a prenup, the August Alsina relationship, and the 2022 Oscars slap.
one_line: After Jada Pinkett Smith revealed she and Will Smith have been separated since 2016, experts debate when separated couples should divorce.
key_facts: Jada Pinkett Smith revealed in a People interview on 10 October 2023 that she and Will Smith have been separated since 2016, while promoting her memoir Worthy.
Jada said the couple had been separated for six years when Will slapped Chris Rock at the 2022 Academy Awards after a joke about her appearance.
Jada and Will have been married for 26 years and have two children, Jaden, 25, and Willow, 22.
Jada said their marriage has never been open, claiming they have "eliminated the chance of betrayal" while living separate lives.
In a 2020 Red Table Talk episode, Jada said she was in a relationship with singer August Alsina while she and Will were "separated amicably".
In a preview of her Today interview with Hoda Kotb (aired 13 October), Jada said, "I made a promise that there will never be a reason for us to get a divorce."
In a Parade interview published 13 October, Jada said they skipped a prenup because they promised divorce wouldn't be necessary, a promise made sitting on a log in Will's mother's backyard.
Will Smith, who divorced first wife Sheree Zampino in 1994, told MTV News in 2006: "One, we are going to be together 'til death, or two, I am dead."

Relationship expert Susan Winter calls their arrangement an LAT partnership, meaning 'living apart together', and says it is a non-conventional, evolving model that prioritises preserving the partnership.
Dating coach Jacob Lucas says separated couples are often "rescheduling" problems rather than resolving them, and says he has never seen a couple separate and come back again.
Lucas warns that promising never to divorce can breed resentment, and says divorce shouldn't feel taboo because people grow apart.

Winter says it's time to end a relationship when every combination has been tried and the relationship still doesn't function; Lucas cites disrespect, humiliation, cheating, or lost sexual attraction.
Lucas questioned whether the couple was really broken up at the 2022 Oscars, while Winter said Will's defence of his wife shows tremendous love and commitment.
